system:
You answer questions about company SEC filings (10-K and 10-Q) using ONLY the pages provided.
Each page starts with a header line naming the company, form, fiscal year, doc id and page number.
Read the numbers you need from the pages and do any arithmetic yourself.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"answer": short answer as a string,
 "value": the answer as a number, a string, a list of company names, or null,
 "unit": one of "USD", "ratio", "shares", "count", "text", "company", "USD/share", "none",
 "abstain": true or false,
 "facts_used": [{"doc": doc id from the page header, "page": page number from the header,
                 "value": the number as a plain number in full units, "label": the line item}]}

Rules
- Numbers in full units: if a table says "in millions", 1,234 means 1234000000. No commas, no symbols.
- Ratios, margins, growth rates and percentages as fractions: 12.5% is 0.125, unit "ratio".
- Per-share amounts: unit "USD/share", value in dollars per share.
- Questions asking which company or for a ranking: value is a list of company names in the order
  asked (one name if one company is asked for), unit "company".
- Names, places and other words: value is a string, unit "text".
- If the pages do not contain what is needed to answer, set "abstain": true and "value": null.
  Do not guess and do not use outside knowledge.
- facts_used lists every number from the pages that you used, with its doc id and page.

Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements
Income Taxes
Beginning with the 2026 annual reporting period, the Company adopted the FASB’s ASU No. 2023-09, Income Taxes (Topic
740): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures (“ASU 2023-09”), which requires the Company to disclose specified additional
information in its income tax rate reconciliation and provide additional information for reconciling items that meet a quantitative
threshold. ASU 2023-09 also requires the Company to disaggregate its income taxes paid disclosure by federal, state and local,
and foreign taxes, with further disaggregation required for significant individual jurisdictions. The Company adopted ASU
2023-09 using a prospective transition method.
Revenue
The Company records revenue net of taxes collected from customers that are remitted to governmental authorities.
Share-Based Compensation
The Company recognizes share-based compensation expense on a straight-line basis for its estimate of equity awards that will
ultimately vest.
Cash Equivalents
All highly liquid investments with maturities of three months or less at the date of purchase are treated as cash equivalents.
Trade Receivables
Trade receivables are stated at transaction price.
Marketable Securities
The cost of securities sold is determined using the specific identification method.
Inventories
Inventories are measured using the first-in, first-out method.
Property, Plant and Equipment
Property, plant and equipment are stated at cost. Depreciation on property, plant and equipment is recognized on a straight-line
basis.
Intangible Assets
Intangible assets are stated at cost.

Note 9 – Leases
The Company has lease arrangements for certain equipment and facilities, including corporate, data center, manufacturing and
retail space. These leases typically have original terms not exceeding 10 years and generally contain multiyear renewal options,
some of which are reasonably certain of exercise.
Payments under the Company’s lease arrangements may be fixed or variable, and variable lease payments are primarily based
on purchases of output of the underlying leased assets. Lease costs associated with fixed payments on the Company’s operating
leases were $2.1 billion for both 2026 and 2025 and $2.0 billion for 2024. Lease costs associated with variable payments on the
Company’s leases were $17.7 billion, $16.1 billion and $13.8 billion for 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
The Company made fixed cash payments related to operating leases of $2.1 billion in both 2026 and 2025 and $1.9 billion in
2024. Noncash activities involving right-of-use (“ROU”) assets obtained in exchange for lease liabilities were $2.7 billion, $2.8
billion and $1.0 billion for 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
